title: Moses on Nebo (Deuteronomy 34)
hookLine: he sees the promised land and dies before entering
last: THE WORD IS VERY NEAR YOU.

cards: An old man climbs a mountain alone. Behind him, in the plains of Moab, a whole people waits. He has walked with them through a sea, a desert, a golden calf, a long run of complaints and a long run of mercies.

At the top of Nebo, God shows him everything: the hills of the north, the far sea in the west, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees. And then God tells him plainly: you have seen it with your eyes.

teach.b: First, why. Back in the book of Numbers, at a place called Meribah, the people were dying of thirst, and God told Moses to speak to a rock. Moses, angry, struck it twice instead.
Water came. But God told him then: you won't bring this people into the land. Readers still argue about why that moment counted so much.
The text doesn't fully explain it. Second, the death.

teach.h: HE DIES AT THE MOUTH OF THE LORD.
teach.b: The text says Moses the servant of the Lord died there, according to the word of the Lord. In Hebrew, literally, at the mouth of the Lord; Jewish tradition came to say God took his soul with a kiss.
He was a hundred and twenty, and his eye was not dim.
God himself buries him, and no one knows his grave to this day. Third, the people. They weep for him thirty days.
Joshua, full of the spirit of wisdom, takes over.
And the book closes: there never arose again a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. Fourth, how the story goes on.
One opinion in the Talmud says Joshua wrote these last verses, since Moses couldn't describe his own burial.
The Gospels bring Moses back once more, on a mountain inside the land, talking with Jesus at the Transfiguration; Luke says they spoke of the exodus Jesus would accomplish in Jerusalem.
And the night before he was killed in 1968, Martin Luther King Junior told a church in Memphis he had been to the mountaintop and seen the promised land, and might not get there with them.

how: Catholics honor Moses as a holy prophet, and pilgrims visit Mount Nebo in Jordan, where a Franciscan-cared-for church and lookout stand over the Jordan valley, though the text says no one knows where Moses is buried.

games.q: you're Moses, a hundred and twenty years old, on top of Nebo. God shows you the whole land you've walked toward for forty years. what happens next?
o: you cross the Jordan and lead them in.
you die there, and God buries you where no one knows.
games.why: he dies on Nebo at the word of the Lord, and God himself buries him. the people weep thirty days, and Joshua leads them on.

practice: Think of something you're working toward that is bigger than your lifetime: a child growing up, a parish, a cause, a family healing that may take generations.

Picture the far end of it; let yourself want it, and gently accept that you may only see it from the mountain. If you pray, entrust it to God, who buried Moses himself; if not, hold it with open hands.

wordCard.voice: Nebo. The mountain where the prophet the Lord knew face to face was shown the whole promised land, and died before he could enter it. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Nebo, the mountain in Moab facing Jericho across the Jordan, where Moses saw the land and died.

carryVoice: Your line: some only see it. Seeing it from the mountain doesn't make your part smaller. Day three hundred eighty-nine.
